project: Multimodal Spatio-Temporal Air Quality Prediction for Indian Urban Environments

primary_reasons: Lack of sub-daily timestamps: PM25Vision records dates only (YYYY-MM-DD), with no hour/minute data, making alignment with 24-hour sequence forecasting impossible without arbitrary hour assignment.
Extreme intraday variance: Station PM2.5 fluctuates by an average of 166.72 ug/m3 (min 85.21 to max 251.93 ug/m3) within a single day at matched sites.
Severe effective sample size bottleneck: Only 265 image-station pairs share a date within 5 km, representing only 36 independent station-date groups across 19 stations over 5.5 years.
Heavy spatial and temporal clustering: 40% of all matched images originate from just two bursts (63 images at DL002 on 2016-01-30 and 42 images at DL026 on 2018-10-24).

Target discrepancy and bias: PM25Vision image labels have an average positive bias of +70.74 ug/m3 relative to CPCB ground monitors (236.83 vs 166.09 ug/m3), reflecting distinct underlying data generation processes.

q4_repeated_images_analysis.finding: Repeated images in a station-date group represent distinct camera captures (distinct SHA-256 hashes) taken in rapid succession at nearly identical GPS coordinates, all sharing the same static PM2.5 label.

recommended_paper_strategy.main_forecasting_model: Numerical LSTM (404,431 test sequences, PM2.5 MAE=10.57, R2=0.949)
recommended_paper_strategy.vision_model_role: Image-only exploratory baseline (ResNet-50 transfer learning, 640 images, Test MAE=66.21, R2=0.152)
recommended_paper_strategy.fusion_conclusion: Rigorous negative result / boundary condition: Opportunistic ground imagery lacking precise sub-daily timestamps cannot defensibly enhance continuous hourly forecasting systems. Future multimodal architectures require synchronized sensor-camera capture networks.
